key_insight: Trotterized quantum simulation can preserve Abelian symmetries when Hamiltonians are written as Hermitian excitation operators, but non-Abelian symmetries need additional structure-preserving tricks.
engineering_relevance: This gives quantum algorithm designers a practical path to reduce symmetry-breaking error in time evolution and quantum phase estimation for chemistry and other fermionic systems.
method: Rewrite Hamiltonian using Hermitian excitation operators
Map operators to sums of commuting Pauli strings that conserve Abelian symmetries
Use operator kirigami: orthogonal projection and unitary folding to better handle non-Abelian symmetry terms
evidence_signal: The authors tested operator pools on small molecules and basis sets, finding electron-number and spin-conserving pools had larger errors that shrank for larger molecules and disappeared with second-order Trotterization.
watch_item: Symmetry preservation is not automatic under Trotterization, especially for non-Abelian symmetries, so implementation choice and Trotter order can materially affect accuracy.
paper_title: Symmetry conservation with Trotterization and Quantum Phase Estimation
